data.about: A uniform line load q on a beam whose two supports can slide inward, leaving overhanging ends. The load is discretized into ten strips on the load line; a funicular polygon from any pole o′ and its closing line give the division point l — the reaction split — while the V-diagram slopes at −q with jumps A and B at the supports. Every ordinate between funicular and closing, scaled by the pole distance H, is the bending moment: M(x) = H · y(x), hogging drawn upward on the tension side.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: a beam of length l = 10 m on two supports A and B — drag them! — the ends overhang; dotted verticals mark the edges and the supports
steps.title: The beam on two supports

steps.caption: left: a uniform line load q covers the whole beam (green band) — right: q = 0.3 kN/m; in total it weighs q · l
steps.title: The line load q

steps.caption: left: cut the load into ten strips of q · 1 m, acting on the dotted station lines — right: the strips laid off tip-to-tail on the load line: a, b, c, … k
steps.title: Discretize into ten strips

steps.caption: left: all strips together are R = q · l acting in the middle of the dimension line — right: R spans the whole load line from a to k
steps.title: The resultant R

steps.caption: right: choose a pole o′ anywhere on the vertical at distance H left of the load line (red segment H below) — H will scale the moment diagram
steps.title: Pole o′ at distance H

steps.caption: right: draw the eleven rays from the load line points to the pole o′
steps.title: Rays a…k → o′

steps.caption: left: from any start FP₀ on the left edge, draw each string parallel to its ray, strip by strip, to the right edge — the funicular of the ten strip loads
steps.title: The funicular polygon

steps.caption: left: extend the FIRST and LAST strings to the support verticals and connect the two points: the dashed closing line — outside the supports it follows the outer strings
steps.title: The closing line

steps.caption: right: the parallel to the closing line through o′ cuts the load line at l — the split of the reactions, the same for any pole and any start
steps.title: Division point l

steps.caption: right: l splits the load line: A = l→a and B = k→l, offset beside it — left: the same forces push up at the supports
steps.title: Reactions A and B

steps.caption: left: a baseline under the beam; the shear starts and ends at ZERO on the free overhanging tips
steps.title: V-diagram — the baseline

steps.caption: left: from the tip the shear falls at slope −q to the support, where the reaction A jumps it up — right: exactly the segment l→a
steps.title: V-diagram — overhang and jump A

steps.caption: left: falling at −q it crosses zero mid-span, jumps by B at the second support, and runs back to zero at the tip — right: the segment k→l
steps.title: V-diagram — span and jump B

steps.caption: left: a second baseline; the moment is also zero at both free tips
steps.title: M-diagram — the baseline

steps.caption: left: at the ten stations and at BOTH supports, measure the ordinate y between the closing polygon and the funicular (grey)
steps.title: Ordinates y between funicular and closing

steps.caption: left: each ordinate scaled by H (× the force scale) and mirrored about the baseline: hogging (closing above funicular) plots UP — the tension side
steps.title: M = H · y

steps.caption: left: connecting the scaled ordinates gives the bending-moment diagram: parabolic sag between the stations, peaks over the supports — try dragging them!
steps.title: The M-diagram

steps.caption: drag the supports, o′, FP₀, N or the load line, tune q and H — everything follows; click a funicular kink (or use the node slider) to read a strip node's equilibrium
steps.title: Internal forces from the funicular
